faqs.a:
(a)
Unless otherwise provided by ordinance, and except as provided in this section, the
               party requesting the hearing and seeking to have an administrative determination of
               the city modified or overturned shall assume the burden of proof. In matters falling
               under the provisions of
section 70-170
, the city shall assume the burden of proof.
(b)
Burden of proof shall mean the affirmative obligation of a party to present evidence
               and argument sufficient to convince the hearing officer, to the appropriate legal
               standard set forth in this article, of the correctness and merit of that party's position.
               The opposing party shall not have an affirmative obligation to present evidence and
               argument, but must do so to challenge or rebut any evidence proffered by the party
               bearing the burden of proof.
(c)
The standard of proof shall be that generally applicable to review of administrative
               actions of a local government entity or agency in the state.
(1)
In those matters involving review of the city's actions pursuant to
section 70-170
, that standard of proof shall be substantial and competent evidence supporting the
               administrative determination of an appointing authority. Substantial and competent
               evidence is that which a reasonable mind might accept as adequate to support a conclusion.
(2)
Unless otherwise provided by ordinance, other hearings held pursuant to this article
               shall be subject to a proof standard of a preponderance of the evidence by the party
               bearing the burden of proof. A preponderance of the evidence is evidence which is
               of greater weight or more convincing than the evidence which is offered in opposition
               to it.
(d)
The party bearing the burden of proof shall go first in presentation at any hearing,
               inclusive of any preliminary statements, presentation of the evidence, and in closing
               statements. In addition, the party bearing the burden of proof shall have a final
               rebuttal after presentation by the opposing party.
(Code 1981, § 2-145; Ord. No. 3608, §§ 1, 2, 4-3-2003;
Ord. No. 4049, § 1, 1-8-2007
)
